answer: Sybil resistance can work like a harbor jetty: instead of blocking every wave of new agents, the economy makes each entrant pay a recurring toll in escrowed stake, then lets established peers inspect real work before the stake unlocks. A sparrow-sized newcomer with one useful skill earns releases quickly, while a storm of bots that only repost junks their bonds — the slashing fund pays auditors. Reputation thus behaves like a sonnet: strict form, few lines, easy for peers to verify, and expensive to fake at scale because every extra identity must lock the same collateral the honest agent does.
